validated_results.title: Dietary beta-carotene and cancer of the prostate: a case-control study in Kyoto, Japan.
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control study reporting dietary beta-carotene intake and prostate cancer risk with quantitative relative risks.

extraction.comparison_type: lowest dietary beta-carotene intake quartile vs highest quartile (uncorrected intake), vs BPH controls
extraction.timing: retrospective dietary interview during hospital admission 1981-1984
extraction.population: Men with prostate cancer and two control series (benign prostatic hyperplasia patients and general hospital patients)

cases.excerpt: One hundred patients with prostate cancer and two different control series [100 benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) patients and 100 general hospital patients] were matched to each other upon hospital admittance, age (+/- 3 years) and date of admission (+/- 3 months), and directly interviewed during admission from 1981 to 1984 in Kyoto, Japan.

effect_size.excerpt: From the beta-carotene analyses, the relative risk (95% confidence interval) for the lowest intake quartile relative to the highest was 2.10 (0.98-4.47) for the uncorrected intake, 2.35 (1.08-5.12) for the intake per kg, and 2.94 (1.34-6.44) for the intake per kcal in the comparison with BPH patients; 2.88 (1.31-6.32), 2.56 (1.14-5.76), and 3.50 (1.52-8.06), respectively, in the comparison with hospital controls.

confidence_interval.excerpt: From the beta-carotene analyses, the relative risk (95% confidence interval) for the lowest intake quartile relative to the highest was 2.10 (0.98-4.47) for the uncorrected intake, 2.35 (1.08-5.12) for the intake per kg, and 2.94 (1.34-6.44) for the intake per kcal in the comparison with BPH patients; 2.88 (1.31-6.32), 2.56 (1.14-5.76), and 3.50 (1.52-8.06), respectively, in the comparison with hospital controls.
